clue.text: Hit and wound horribly, leading to murder investigation

indicators.note: something done horribly is botched and mangled, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A violent attack leaves a victim badly hurt, and the police open a murder inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only a joining word: the fodder is HIT plus WOUND, eight letters, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story centred on solving a killing, so a murder investigation in fiction.

clue.text: Dwelling overheated-resort to thin wrap inside

indicators.note: pieces put inside another sit within its letters

parts.note: something overheated is hot
to resort to something is to use it
a boa is a long thin scarf of feathers or fur

explanation.surface: In an overheated house someone resorts to wearing only a thin wrap.
explanation.walkthrough: A boa here is a feather stole, not the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseboat is a boat fitted out to be lived in, so a home or dwelling.

clue.text: River overrunning low-lying land initially checked by barricade

indicators.note: a river that overruns land spreads around it, so the river's letters surround the rest

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a fen is low-lying marshy land

indicators.note: initially says take only the first letter of checked

explanation.surface: A river floods the fens and is first held back by a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A defence is a protective barrier or fortification, much as a barricade is.

clue.text: Came first to lock house up? Certainly not!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to come first in a contest is to win, past tense won

explanation.surface: The winner locks up the house: no chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole assembly backwards, as a down entry is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Nohow is a dialect or jocular word for in no way at all, an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: Yank has to draw up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to draw a fowl is to gut it, taking out the innards

explanation.surface: An American has to pull something upward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' is not an American but a verb meaning to pull sharply; 'has to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To yank is to pull hard and suddenly, and a tug is the same action.

clue.text: Comb that's brown (chestnut)

parts.note: to sear meat is to brown it quickly in a hot pan
CH is the standard abbreviation for chestnut, the horse colour

explanation.surface: A description of a comb that happens to be brown, the colour of a chestnut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link word. CH for chestnut is a horse-racing abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area is to search it thoroughly, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Gin drunk at first, and another spirit — 9 could come from this

parts.note: a gin is a trap for animals, a snare

indicators.note: at first says take the first letter of drunk

parts.note: rum is another alcoholic spirit besides gin

explanation.surface: A drinker downs gin and then moves on to another spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink, but it is a snare or trap. 9 is RUFF, a drummer's roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruff is a low vibrating beat played on a drum, typically the side drum with wires underneath.

clue.text: Shortly to receive medal, etc

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon or shortly
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military decoration

explanation.surface: A soldier is about to receive a medal, and so forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Etc, short for et cetera, means the same as the phrase meaning and so forth.

clue.text: Near the end

explanation.surface: Close to the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Close as an adjective means nearby, and as a noun means the conclusion of something.

clue.text: Fish with frill round neck

definitions.meaning: a small freshwater perch-like fish goes by this name
the stiff pleated collar worn in Elizabethan times

explanation.surface: A fish sporting an ornamental collar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a small perch-like fish and a starched pleated Elizabethan collar.

clue.text: Up and down, all over the place

parts.note: up means high
down means low

explanation.surface: Something moving up and down and scattered everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Searching high and low is an idiom for looking everywhere, all over the place.

clue.text: Receive two presents, but make no progress

parts.note: to receive is to get
the present in time is now; the present in place is here
the present in time is now; the present in place is here

explanation.surface: Someone receives a pair of gifts but is still stuck in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presents' is not gifts but two senses of 'present': now (the present moment) and here (present in this place).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'get nowhere' means to fail to advance or achieve anything.

clue.text: Just this Latin, and others on the outside

indicators.note: one piece on the outside of another wraps around it

parts.note: et al is Latin shorthand for and others
hic is Latin for this

explanation.surface: A remark about a Latin phrase, with other phrases surrounding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' is not 'only' but an adjective meaning fair and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair and morally right, the same as principled conduct.

clue.text: Period of play is finished

definitions.meaning: in cricket a set of six balls bowled from one end
done or at an end, as in 'the game is finished'

explanation.surface: A game session has come to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler; 'is' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: An over is a cricket term for a unit of play, and 'over' also means ended or done.

clue.text: Black medick, a thing unequalled in olden days

definitions.meaning: a small clover-like plant with yellow flowers, also called hop clover

definitions.text: a thing unequalled in olden days
definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a person or thing without equal

explanation.surface: A plant once regarded as peerless.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dictionary senses: a name for the plant black medick, and an archaic term for something without parallel.

clue.text: Using wind power in laundries? That's unusual

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of these letters is a different order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders at laundries running on wind energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat under sail is propelled by the wind in its sails.

clue.text: For fun, playing tie-breaker

indicators.note: playing about with the letters suggests rearranging them freely

explanation.surface: Someone playing a deciding match just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-off is a deciding race or vote held after a tie, so a tie-breaker.

clue.text: Jack may be seen here — man sustaining plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the lower piece holds up, or sustains, the one on top

parts.note: a flag is an iris, a plant
to man a place is to staff it

explanation.surface: A man holding up a plant, where a Jack is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is not a man but a small flag on a ship, the Union Jack's namesake.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is a ship's flag, and a flagstaff is the pole from which such a flag flies.

clue.text: From shore, rook enters group of trees

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it

parts.note: a stand is a group of growing trees
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook flies from the shore into a copse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' is a link word; 'rook' is not the bird but the chess piece, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A strand is a literary word for a beach or shore.

clue.text: Waste a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize awarded for winning

explanation.surface: Giving out a prize would be wasteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is a wasting away of a body part, so to waste is the verb sense.

clue.text: Hope, perhaps, to get together business centre

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a median is a middle or central value or line

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to bring together a central business district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hope' is not wishing but Bob Hope, the comedian; 'perhaps' marks him as an example. 'to get together' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Hope was a famous American comic, an example of the class.

clue.text: Woody core of the French/Japanese soup

parts.note: du is French for of the
ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A soup with a woody core, part French and part Japanese.
explanation.definitionFit: Duramen is the botanical term for heartwood, the hard central part of a tree trunk.

clue.text: Some children's parents fight

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some mothers and fathers of children quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across the end of children's and the start of parents.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue in a sparring way, a synonym for fight.

clue.text: Procurator has dropped one horseshoe

parts.note: Pontius Pilate was the Roman procurator of Judaea
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An official has lost one horseshoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A plate is a light shoe fitted to a racehorse.

clue.text: Motor sport involving lorry class

indicators.note: involve in its old sense is to roll up or entangle, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A motoring competition that includes a class for lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' looks like a link word, but in its sense of entangling it signals the anagram of LORRY CLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallycross is a form of motor racing on a mixed tarmac and loose-surface circuit.

clue.text: Long period before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time ending at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply places one piece ahead of the other; 'Long' is the verb meaning to crave, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to crave it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: There's lots of water here, in case a spa needs a change

indicators.note: letters that need a change are to be rearranged into a different order

explanation.surface: A spa resort in need of a makeover, with plenty of water about.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caspian Sea is the largest inland body of water on Earth, so a place with much water.

clue.text: Bribe offered by some other parties' leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Political party leaders are offered a bribe.
explanation.definitionFit: A sop is a concession or small payment given to placate someone, so a bribe.

clue.text: Poor design

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to intend or plan, as in 'I designed it as a gift'

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a piece of design work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can be an adjective for shabby or inferior, and a verb meaning to intend or purpose.

clue.text: Gertrude, gardener and doctor

definitions.meaning: Gertrude ... was a celebrated English garden designer
The scientist of Stevenson's tale of a split personality

explanation.surface: A woman called Gertrude who both gardens and practises medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the Victorian garden designer Gertrude and to Stevenson's fictional doctor.

clue.text: Cutter in covered dock taking on three metals

parts.note: a pen is a covered dock, as for submarines
K is potassium, Ni is nickel and Fe is iron by their chemical symbols
K is potassium, Ni is nickel and Fe is iron by their chemical symbols
K is potassium, Ni is nickel and Fe is iron by their chemical symbols

explanation.surface: A shipyard cutter in a covered dock takes on a load of three metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' suggests a boat, matching the dock, but it is a small knife. 'taking on' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A penknife is a small folding blade, a tool for cutting.
